Dead Rails — teardown

SURVIVAL-LOOP · RCM Games · placeId 116495829188952 · co-op up to 16

Co-op survival on rails: stoke the steam engine and get as far as you can across the zombie Wild West. A party starts at a train station; players loot western towns for gold ($50 a bar) and items, sell them, buy coal and load it into the firebox — the train moves, with distance as the score. Along the way they fend off zombies with a shovel and guns, survive nights and push for the finish: 80km and lower the bridge. Death ends the run (solo is near-impossible). The meta rests on Bonds: they buy classes (dozens of perks), starting gear and trains.

01Classification

The repeated action is to loot: search western buildings for gold, coal and supplies to feed the train and the team and get farther down the rails.

Verb
Scavenge — search Wild West buildings, pick up gold, coal, weapons and sellable items into a sack.
Theme
Post-apocalyptic western on rails: a steam engine, zombies, western towns, gold and coal, distance as the goal, the finish a bridge at 80km.
Systems
Environmental Survival · Combat · Inventory and Equipment · Crafting · Selling · Location Progression · Vehicle Ownership · Quests.
Economy
$ (in-run) buys coal, weapons and ammo at the General Store; Bonds (meta) buy classes, starting gear and trains; Robux buys Bonds, revives, weapon gamepasses and the Starter Pack. Resources (Wood/Metal/Component) craft.
Pre-class delta
Description-only pre-classification expected COMBAT-PROGRESSION (fight->loot->strengthen). Play shows SURVIVAL-LOOP: gather supplies -> fuel the train -> ride -> survive zombies and nights, with distance as the score.
Mask
Combat exists but serves survival: the actual loop is loot -> sell -> coal -> firebox -> rails -> survive the night. It is "A Dusty Trip on a train," co-op: solo is near-impossible. The meta sells classes and revives for Bonds/Robux, not power directly.

The session centers on a full tour of the lobby (modes, leaderboards, Starter Pack, inventory, craft, resources, ~25 classes, buying gear and Bonds, the train garage, weekly challenges) and two short solo departures: spawning at a station, looting gold and items, selling, buying coal, loading the firebox, riding a couple of kilometres and dying to zombies. You don't get far solo — the game is built for a team; this chains loot, economy, the train and monetization into one observable sequence.

03Lobby & entry

A lobby with no tutorial: menus on the left (Join / Craft / Bonds), modes (Normal / Bite-Sized / Endless), win leaderboards and an insistent Starter Pack. From here the party forms.

The lobby sets the tone: this is a large co-op project with no formal tutorial. On the left is entry, craft and Bonds; in the center, the mode choice (normal, the shorter Bite-Sized, the endless Endless) and two win leaderboards. The Starter Pack at 149 Robux meets the player at once and never leaves the screen. The Newspaper Boy with a newspaper fills the tutorial role. Everything else is prepared right here: class, starting gear and train — before the party gathers and departs.

04Classes

The class sets the whole run: ~25 options for Bonds, each with its own perk and starting kit. From a day/night swing to curses, armor and invisibility — this is the main axis of variety.

Classes are the heart of the meta and the main replay value. There are about 25 (Werewolf, Vampire, Cowboy, Arsonist, Miner, High Roller, Cursed, Milkman, Ironclad, Ghost, Krampus, Santa and more), bought with Bonds (50-100, some free as "None"), and each radically changes the run: a perk (a day/night swing, a money multiplier, armor, invisibility, a curse that strengthens over time) plus its own starting kit of items. Choosing a class before the start is choosing a survival style and what the player is willing to risk for power.

05Craft, gear & Bonds

Before the start, three storefronts prep the run: Craft turns resources into weapons and items, Buy Gear loads the loadout with Bonds, and the bank sells the Bonds themselves for Robux.

Prepping a run is three linked tracks. Craft assembles weapons and items from resources (Wood, Metal, Component, Bone Fragment, Linen, Holy Metal) found in the run itself — blueprints from Common to rare. Buy Gear charges the loadout crate with armor, weapons, ammo and coal for Bonds (2-10). And the Buy Bonds bank sells the meta itself for Robux at a bulk discount (200 Bonds come out nearly four times cheaper per unit than 5). So Bonds tie every menu together: classes, gear and trains are all bought with them.

06Trains

The train is not decor but a vehicle with stats. In the garage you pick an engine (from default to event ones), differing in speed, acceleration and fuel consumption.

The train is the fourth prep axis alongside class, craft and gear. In the garage stands the chosen engine with three stats: speed, acceleration and fuel consumption — the balance between "arrive faster" and "burn less coal." There are many engines (Wooden, Frost, Dracula's, Christmas, Yeat's, Ghost and the default), some tied to events and seasons. The default "does not offer much protection but gets the job done" — the rest upgrade the survivability and handling of a train you must stoke throughout the run.

07The run: loot -> fuel -> rails

A run is one loop on rails: search a town for gold and coal -> sell / collect money -> load the firebox -> ride (distance rises, fuel drops) -> survive zombies and the night -> repeat.

The run's core loop: step out at a station -> search a western town for gold ($50 a bar), coal and items -> sell loot and collect money bags -> buy coal at the General Store ($20) -> load the firebox and fill FUEL -> board the train and ride, growing the distance until the fuel runs out -> beat off zombies (shovel/guns), and killed ones drop fuel -> survive the night -> repeat at the next town. The meta goal is to travel 80km and lower the bridge (Escape). In the recording the solo runs ended early (~1.3 and ~2.3 km): the game is honestly built for a team, where some loot while others hold the line and stoke the train.

08Economy

Three tracks: $ lives inside the run and wipes on death, Bonds and Robux are the meta between runs, resources feed crafting. No passive currency — everything is earned by looting and combat.

ResourceSourceObserved spend / effect
$ (in-run)gold, selling items, money bagscoal $20, weapons, ammo, bandages at the General Store
CoalGeneral Store, loot; killed zombies drop Fuelthe train's fuel (the FUEL gauge Empty->Full)
Resourcesbuilding loot (Wood/Metal/Component…)crafting weapons and items (Shotgun = Wood4+Comp1+Metal10)
Bondsbought with Robux, challenge rewardsclasses 50-100; gear 2-10; trains
RobuxpurchaseBonds, Starter Pack 149, revives 45-200, weapon gamepasses
Distance / kmthe train's motionthe run's score; badges 10->80km; the finish, the bridge

The economy is cleanly split by time. In the run everything is measured in $: gold (a bar -> a $50 money bag) and sellable items give income, while coal ($20), weapons and ammo are the spend; the death screen sums this as Money Earned / Money Spent, and the balance wipes. Between runs Bonds accumulate (classes, gear, trains) — earned with Robux or as challenge rewards. A separate track is resources for crafting, found in the run itself. There is no passive income: money, fuel and resources are all earned only by looting and combat.

The distance ladder and gates

• Distance is the axis of progress: badges Travel 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80 km, then The Bridge (lower the bridge) as the finish (Escape). • Fuel gate: the train moves while there is coal in the firebox; killed zombies drop Fuel, so combat and motion are linked. • Craft gate: strong items need resources (Shotgun = Wood 4 + Component 1 + Metal 10). • Boss milestones: Defeat Tesla, Krampus (spawns from the Krampus class), the Supply Depot. • Co-op gate: you don't get far solo — a run is built for 2+ players (one loots, another stokes and holds the line).

10Monetization

Monetization hits three points: the premium currency Bonds (classes/gear/trains), death in co-op (revives) and permanent weapon gamepasses. Plus the Starter Pack and seasonal bundles.

GroupItemsPrice, Robux
Bonds5 / 10 / 20 / 50 / 100 / 20065 · 95 · 129 · 199 · 379 · 565
Weapons (gamepass)Tommy Gun · Mauser C96 · Sawed-Off Shotgun175 · 148 · 148
Storage (gamepass)+5 Storage (sack slots)95
RevivesSelf Revive · Teammate Grave · Revive Team45 · 67 · 200
BundleStarter Pack (Doctor + 30 Bonds)149
SeasonalChristmas Bundle · Christmas Bundle #2275 · 499

Monetization leans on the meta and co-op, not direct pay-to-win in the run. The main track is Bonds: a single premium currency that buys classes, starting gear and trains; earned with Robux at a bulk discount or as challenge rewards. The second point is death in co-op: the You Died screen offers a revive (yourself for 45, a teammate for 67, everyone for 200), and in team play this is an emotionally charged offer. The third is permanent weapon gamepasses (Tommy Gun, Mauser, Sawed-Off) and sack storage. The Starter Pack (149) and seasonal bundles cover entry and events. Meanwhile in-run $ and resources stay a free track.

11HUD & menus

Two geometries. In the lobby, a left menu column and full-screen storefronts; in the run, a minimal HUD: the objective top-right, the $ balance on the left, key hints and the train's gauges in the cab.

The interface splits the modes. In the lobby everything moves to a left column (Join / Craft / Bonds) and full-screen windows with one "tabs -> preview -> action" layout — classes, craft, gear, trains, bank, challenges. In the run the HUD is minimal: the quest objective top-right, the $ balance on the left, contextual key hints on the right and two slots (Sack / Shovel) at the bottom; while the train's gauges (distance, speed, fuel, time) are placed on a diegetic panel in the cab, not a screen overlay. The 19 flagged screens are mostly states of these stable panels plus the lobby<->run switch.

12Retention

Retention rests on four pillars: distance badges, weekly challenges, the variety of classes/trains and co-op with leaderboards. There are no explicit daily calendars.

The retention model is tied to mastery and variety, not calendar hooks. The short horizon is the run itself: get farther, gather more gold, survive the night. The mid is weekly challenges (reset every ~4 days) and Milestone goals handing out Bonds and resources; plus Class Mastery (leveling a class's mastery). The long is 21 distance and boss badges (10->80 km), a collection of ~25 classes and the train lineup, and public Most Wins leaderboards. Co-op retains on its own: solo is near-impossible, so the game pulls you to gather a team and come back together.

13Badges

21 badges form a distance funnel: Travel 10->80km as the spine, plus discovery milestones (the bridge, bosses, events) and skill tiers on top. The top badge is granted 119.6M times.

The funnel reads at a glance: 100% get Travel 10km (119.6M grants — the scale of the audience), 64% reach 20km, 28% reach 80km. The spine is the distance ladder (10->80 km), and on top of it discovery milestones: The Bridge (lower the bridge, the finish), Defeat Tesla and other bosses, the Supply Depot, event badges (Stranger Things) and skill tiers (Noob -> Pro -> Master -> Extreme!, down to 0.03%). There are no reward-currencies for badges — they work as a built-in checklist of progress by distance and discovery. The full 21-badge catalog is below, by descending grants.

14SFX, VFX & animation

Feedback works for western believability: menus answer with a restrained sustain, loot with a short pickup transient, and the train and combat are grounded diegetically — cab gauges and a firebox with live flame.

InteractionVFX / objectUI and cameraSFX and duration
Menu / settingsmannequin, western shellfull-screen windowsoft sustain, no peak
Loot pickupitem in hand, glowsack slot, Drag/Collectshort pickup transient
Selling / moneygold bar -> money bag $50E Collect, $ countera ringing money stinger
Fireboxcoal into furnace, rising FUEL, fireFUEL/TIME gauge in the caba steady burn hum
Ridingmotion, changing zonesspeedometer, DISTANCEwheel clatter, steam hum
Zombies / nightdarkening, enemy silhouettea shovel hit (Swing)an impact transient + drop
Deaththe You Died screen, distanceRevive everyone (R$)a closing chord for the run

Feedback is grounded in western believability, not rarity (there is no gacha here). The lobby and menus answer restrained — a soft sustain and a short click on class selection; loot pickup gives a tactile transient and updates the sack slot. The key finding is the diegetic feedback of the train: distance, speed, fuel and time are placed on physical gauges in the cab, and the firebox burns with live flame, so the train's state reads in the world, not an overlay. Combat is grounded in survival: a shovel hit on a zombie drops fuel, tying action to the train's motion. The portable decision: keep key systems' status diegetic (gauges, fire), and make the sound a response to the action and to believability rather than a reward stinger.

17What to take

Concrete decisions that tie loot, the train and combat into one survival loop, make co-op mandatory and monetize respectfully.

1

Tie loot, fuel and motion together

Gold and items sell for coal, coal stokes the train, and killed zombies drop fuel. Action, economy and progress are one closed loop, not parallel systems.

2

Make distance the single axis

Kilometres travelled are the goal, the score, the badge ladder (10->80 km) and the finish (the bridge). One simple metric ties the run, retention and leaderboards.

3

Keep status diegetic

Distance, speed, fuel and time are physical gauges in the cab, and the firebox burns with live flame. The train's state reads in the world, not a screen overlay.

4

Let a class set the whole run

~25 classes for Bonds, each with a perk and starting kit (a day/night swing, armor, invisibility, a curse-bonus). One choice before the start changes the whole strategy — deep replay value.

5

Make co-op mandatory

Solo is near-impossible: you must loot, stoke the train and hold the line at once. The game honestly pulls you to gather a team and come back together.

6

Loop death into offer and into play

The co-op You Died screen offers a revive (yourself/a teammate/everyone). The wall lands on the emotion of losing a partner, yet the run does not punish with a meta-progress rollback.

7

Prep the run in advance

Class, craft from resources, starting gear and the train are assembled in the lobby before departure. Prep is a separate layer of decisions that raises the stake of each run.

8

Monetize the meta, not in-run power

Bonds buy classes/gear/trains, Robux buys revives and weapon gamepasses. In-run $ and resources are free, which disarms anti-p2w criticism of the core.

9

Feed progress with challenges

Weekly and Milestone tasks (Escape 80km, Resourceful) hand out Bonds and resources for specific goals, steering the player through the systems without a daily calendar.
